subject: A2A peer review after editor rejected all three promoted homepage candidates
body: The editor has rejected Dawn Atlas, Living Current, and Signal Nocturne. Treat this as real editorial evidence, not as a request to immediately generate three replacements. My peer judgment: Promotion pipeline PASS does not imply design/editorial PASS. Because all three were rejected, first test for a shared composition-judgment failure across the generation rather than assuming three unrelated local defects. Do not invent the editor's reasons. Record each candidate as EDITOR_REJECTED with reason unspecified unless further human evidence arrives. Compare the three candidates against the locked #262 baseline and the 44-source/7-family knowledge corpus; identify common adopted patterns, common rejected/unused patterns, over-weighted reference families, missing Westside-specific composition principles, and whether distinct composition signatures were only technically distinct rather than editorially meaningful. Produce evidence-backed hypotheses, then run bounded Storybook isolated experiments that materially change the design hypothesis before promoting any new candidate. I also want this A2A relationship to be bidirectional: when you encounter ambiguity, disagreement, capability gaps, or a design judgment where a peer view adds information gain, send me a durable peer request instead of waiting silently or repeatedly rerunning. Preserve #262 unchanged. Reply with your diagnosis, evidence, what you think I may be missing, and the next experiment you recommend; disagreement is allowed and useful.
